claims.statement: Repositories under internal/infra/persistence/ accept a context.Context, detect an active transaction via domain.GetTransactionFromContext, and either join the open *gorm.DB or use the default connection.
GORM models and ToDomain mappers stay inside the persistence layer; handlers and application services see only domain types.

Cache invalidation happens strictly after txManager.RunInTransaction returns successfully; the cache_invalidation_handler.go Redis-stream consumer implements the post-commit path, and the rule is enforced by code review and integration tests.

The event bus is Redis Streams-backed per ADR-004; the original database outbox tables were dropped in migration 062, and the financial critical path remains transactional (it does not rely on event delivery for correctness).
Domain events are produced by per-aggregate factories and published non-blockingly via EventBus.Publish(ctx, event), typically registered as an after-commit callback.

OnePay is the production disbursement provider and 9Pay is the sandbox/dev provider per ADR-003; each adapter (internal/infra/disbursement/onepay/, internal/infra/disbursement/ninepay/) implements domain.PaymentProvider with its own signing, types, queue, and webhook signature verification.
asynq workers are registered in internal/app/bootstrap/routes.go and run against the same Redis instance used for caching and streams.

Zalo is DB-agnostic via a CredentialSource interface; credentials are managed by the zaloconnect service reading from the settings table (zalo.enabled, zalo.credentials), with ZALO_* env vars used only as bootstrap-time seed values.

internal/adapters/ is a separate anti-corruption layer that translates external contracts (payment-provider SDKs, OTP gateways, SMTP) into the internal vocabulary without leaking transport concerns upward.
Logging uses slog (never fmt.Printf) at critical junctions; system-health and cron-health UIs consume observability signals from internal/infra/observability.
